title: Can Street Trees Cool a Commercial Block?
text:
Source A - Plant a Test Corridor
A university team measured afternoon surface temperatures on eight commercial blocks. Blocks with mature tree cover averaged 5 degrees Celsius cooler on sunny days than blocks with little shade. The researchers caution that building height and pavement type also affect temperature. They recommend a one-block tree-planting pilot with temperature monitoring before a larger investment.

Source B - Use Shade Sails Instead
A business owner argues that trees grow too slowly and says shade sails would provide immediate cover. She points to one cafe patio where a sail lowered the temperature beneath the fabric. She does not report measurements from the rest of the block or compare installation and maintenance costs. She says the city should therefore choose sails for the entire commercial district.
